rows.title: State agencies’ failure to coordinate quickly led to summer food aid delay
rows.standfirst: Coordination among state agencies took ‘longer than anticipated,’ resulting in CT missing the June deadline, officials acknowledged Monday.

rows.title: Could CT fight homelessness with a ‘mansion tax’? Yes, report says
rows.standfirst: A new report says CT could raise millions to fight homelessness from expensive home sales. Lawmakers could renew ‘mansion tax’ debate in 2025.

rows.title: CT workers enjoy healthy raises despite ‘fiscal guardrails’
rows.standfirst: Some officials argue CT should clamp down on state employee raises, which average 4.5% annually. Others say excessive savings are the issue.

rows.title: ‘Unconscionable’: CT SNAP benefit thefts surge by 1,800%
rows.standfirst: Reported EBT thefts — which commonly involve skimming devices placed on a point of sale device — grew from 177 in January to 2,855 in June.

rows.title: Lamont spares higher ed from efficiency cuts to balance CT budget
rows.standfirst: The Lamont administration has charged CT colleges with not doing enough to cut costs, but it won’t ask them to sacrifice over the next year.

rows.title: CT now sitting on $4.1 billion budget reserve
rows.standfirst: With Connecticut’s rainy day fund now projected to approach $4.1 billion, calls to reassess the state’s savings programs continue to grow.

rows.title: The fight for tax breaks for CT families in 2025 is underway
rows.standfirst: Tax reform advocates are zeroing in on a popular concept from the past few years: a CT income tax credit for households with children.

rows.title: Poll: 63% of voters want CT to save less, spend more on services
rows.standfirst: Most likely CT voters would spend more on services, health and education, according to a poll the Lamont administration said is ‘biased.’
